subject: OrionHealth — decisioning: chat vs completions + streaming semantics
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sandeep Rao <sandeep@orionhealth.com>, Elena Martinez <elena@orionhealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 04 Mar 2028 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: OrionHealth discovery — post-call recap and open schema questions

Hi Sandeep / Elena,

Thanks again for taking the call this morning. Quick recap + a few follow-ups so we can scope the POC and give a clean recommendation on API shape and infra. High level notes below, then questions.

Recap (90-minute discovery):
- Primary use: clinician triage assistant embedded in Orion EMR; short-turn prompts, mix of structured tool calls and free-text chat.
- Traffic profile: expected 1.5k concurrent sessions at peak; median request size ~200 tokens, some long context threads (~2,500 tokens).
- SLOs: 95th pct latency under 600ms for interactive flows, batch reranks can be up to 5s.
- Security: VPC peering for Private deployment, audit logs required, customer-managed KMS.

Open technical questions we flagged:
1) Chat vs completions API: when to use streaming chat API vs single-call completions for your flows (we sketched trade-offs below).
2) Tokenization and max_tokens: how you want truncated contexts handled and safe-stop behavior for clinical templates.
3) Streaming semantics & tool-calling: whether you need partial structured outputs or final atomic JSON payloads only.
4) Reranker/embeddings flow: where do you want embeddings produced (client vs server), and reranker scoring latency targets.

Starter recommendations (engineer-facing):
- Use chat-style convs (with streaming) for interactive triage where partial answers are useful; use completions for single-shot templated extractions.
- Enforce prefix tokens for clinical templates and set stop sequences to the template delimiter to avoid hallucinated closures.
- Run embedding generation server-side in Redwood Dedicated/Private to keep patient data contained; reranker can be local to the cluster for sub-100ms scoring.

Concrete asks / next steps:
- Please confirm: are the long-context sessions (2.5k tokens) expected to be sent in full, or can we rely on prefix summarization?
- Share one example prompt + desired structured output schema (I attached a proto schema draft — orion-proto-schema-v1.json).
- Can we schedule a 60-min technical deep dive next Tue (Mar 7) with your infra lead to discuss VPC/KMS requirements?

Attaching: orion-proto-schema-v1.json (example structured output), redwood-integration-checklist.pdf

Thanks — happy to jump on a call if useful.

Best,
Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Sandeep Rao <sandeep@orionhealth.com>

Date: Mon, 06 Mar 2028 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: OrionHealth discovery — post-call recap and open schema questions

Thanks Ben — helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side below.

On long-context sessions: we currently keep full session histories for up to 30 days for auditability, but the UI only displays the last ~500 tokens. For AI assists, we'd prefer Redwood to handle smart prefixing (summarize older context) unless you recommend otherwise.

Chat vs completions: most of our flows are multi-turn with tool calls (patient lookup, meds check) and we want intermediate results surfaced in the UI as they arrive (so streaming looks attractive). That said, for final structured outputs (e.g., discharge summary extract) we want an atomic JSON payload to persist to our records. Question: can the streaming chat API provide safe partial JSON fragments without risking JSON corruption if a token stream is interrupted?

Tokenization/max_tokens: can you recommend how to set max_tokens for streaming responses when the input context may vary? We worry about abrupt truncation in the middle of a structured field.

Reranker/embeddings: we plan to host the vector DB in our VPC but would like Redwood to generate embeddings via an API call that stays inside the Private deployment. Target latency for rerank scoring is ~120ms P95. Is that feasible?

Happy to take the deeper design session — Tue works for our infra lead.

—Sandeep
Head of Product, OrionHealth
S: +1 650-555-0122

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sandeep Rao <sandeep@orionhealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Elena Martinez <elena@orionhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 06 Mar 2028 11:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: OrionHealth discovery — post-call recap and open schema questions

Sandeep — great questions. Short answers first, then specifics and a proposed POC plan.

1) Streaming partial JSON safety: Redwood streaming supports two approaches:
   a) Delimited atomic messages: emit complete JSON objects only (runtime buffers until object close). Streaming is used to signal progress but we only deliver the full JSON when finished. This avoids corrupted records for persistence but adds a tiny buffer delay.
   b) Incremental fragments with robust framing: we can stream JSON fragments with explicit framing tokens and a checksum/frame-id so clients can reassemble safely. This is heavier on client-side logic but shows partial data in UI sooner.

Recommendation: for clinical persistence, use (a) — stream status/notes for UX, but persist only when the runtime returns the final atomic JSON. For exploratory assistants, (b) works if you want early field-level visibility.

2) Tokenization/max_tokens guidance:
- Use dynamic max_tokens: set an upper bound for the model response (e.g., 1024) and implement soft-truncation rules server-side (Redwood supports prefix-preserving truncation).
- For structured outputs, include an explicit end-of-record stop sequence (e.g., "\n===END_RECORD===\n") that prevents mid-field truncation. If a model reaches max_tokens before emitting the stop token, we will set a status code in the response indicating truncation and include the partial JSON plus a flag.

3) Embeddings & reranker latency: Private deployment + server-side embedding generation is supported. With colocated VPC DB and Dedicated GPU pool, P95 embedding generation + rerank scoring at ~120ms is achievable for single-vector fetch + cosine scoring if we use an optimized vector runtime and batch requests intelligently. We recommend a small dedicated pool for that workload.

Proposed POC plan (timeline):
- Phase 1 (1 week): exchange example prompts & desired JSON schema (we have orion-proto-schema-v1.json attached; please annotate fields you require).
- Phase 2 (2 weeks): Redwood provisions a Private trial with a small dedicated pool in us-west; we deploy a sample integration that demonstrates streaming chat with atomic final payload persistence and server-side embedding generation.
- Phase 3 (1 week): Run 1k synthetic concurrent sessions to validate latency and truncation semantics; tune batching and prefix summarization.

Next steps:
- Can your team annotate the attached schema with required vs optional fields and a sample target record?
- Confirm Tue Mar 7 10am PT for a technical deep dive (I’ll send a calendar invite once you confirm + attendee list).

I attached a short README in the schema file with framing examples for both streaming strategies.

Best,
Ben
